newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU SEES POSSIBLE 9.0 MLN T 97/98 WHEAT EXPORTS.
newsitem.headline: EU SEES POSSIBLE 9.0 MLN T 97/98 WHEAT EXPORTS.

text.p: The European Union could export some nine million tonnes of soft wheat in 1997/98 (July/June) if it maintains the current rhythm and favourable export conditions continue, Commission sources said.
Rejecting trade criticism that last week's hike in wheat export taxes signalled a clampdown on shipments, the sources that some 800,000 tonnes had been approved since the season started on July 1.
They suggested that 800,000 tonnes a month was a feasible and not an over-aggressive target.
A strong dollar, firm world prices and buoyant demand, especially from near-East and North African countries, created a favourable export outlook.

Plentiful supplies were expected with another huge EU grain harvest in prospect although there were fears about quality, especially of spring sown crops, following a long spell of wet weather in June and early July.
However a heat wave in recent weeks had improved quality prospects, the sources said, adding that there was still big potential demand for cheaper feed quality wheat and barley.
